messages.author: 72848d54e6872c86
messages.subject: marginals.fixed: y value
parts: Maybe this is a silly question, but I can't understand the value of the y-axis when I plot the marginals.fixed output. I get this is related to the variable's range of values, but what is the exact interpretation? Thanks

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] marginals.fixed: y value
parts:
On Wed, 2017-10-11 at 03:58 -0700, Matteo Scortichini wrote:
> Maybe this is a silly question, but I can't understand the value of
> the y-axis when I plot the marginals.fixed output. I get this is
> related to the variable's range of values, but what is the exact
> interpretation? Thanks

its simply the marginal density values, just plot 'x' against 'y'

> r = inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y=1:10))
> plot(r$marginals.fixed$'(Intercept)')
> lines(inla.smarginal(r$marginals.fixed$'(Intercept)'))


--
Håvard Rue

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] marginals.fixed: y value
parts:
No, the marginal _density_ values are not constrained to [0,1].

PS.
The (slightly informal) units of a density is "probability per x-unit"; not "probability".

Finn
